cross_market_insights: All four markets show the same weak page one: a hotel group's weddings page, Pinterest pins (one from 2020), hotel lists (Ellwed, Tripadvisor, TravelTriangle) and Greek planner blogs. No result in the top 3 is a complete planning overview, and none is written for Australians.

Google's AI Overview answers the query as a planning overview: islands vs mainland (Santorini, Mykonos, Crete, Corfu, Naxos, Athens), season April to November, a EUR budget range, and 'many couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony'. The page that wins is the one that structures exactly that, with sources.

AU and UK AI Overviews give different budget figures (AU: EUR 25,000 to 40,000+ for 50 to 70 guests; UK: EUR 10,000 to 35,000 average, Santorini EUR 40,000 to 70,000 for 100 guests). Budgets in the SERP are unsourced aggregator numbers in EUR only; nobody gives AUD or a dated, attributed range.

The London SERP leans on UK package operators (TUI, ABTA-bonded specialists); Australian SERPs lean on hotels and directories. Neither has Australian legal steps (DFAT CNI, apostilles, recognition in Australia), Smartraveller, flights and transit from Australia, or guest care for older relatives.

PAA in AU: 'How much do destination weddings cost in Greece?' Related searches push packages and all-inclusive (owned on our site by /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages and /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive).
Several ranking and AI Overview sources are blocked for us (The Knot, Reddit as a source, competitor planners and package operators). Research only; never link.
payload.recommended_angle: The Australian couple's planning overview for a Greek destination wedding: choose the island or mainland base, the month, the legal route (marry in Greece with a DFAT CNI, or legally at home plus a symbolic ceremony), a dated budget, and how guests get from Australia, then hand off to our deeper spoke pages. Show the invisible work a Wedded Wonderland advisor handles (ferries and wind, transfers, steps for older guests, room blocks, EUR payments). This is the hub-and-spoke page the SERP and our own site are both missing.
